events.title: Nero becomes Roman emperor at 16
events.description: On the death of Claudius, reputedly poisoned by his wife Agrippina, her 16-year-old son Nero was proclaimed emperor. His reign began promisingly but ended in tyranny, rebellion and his suicide in 68.
events.html: On the death of Claudius, reputedly poisoned by his wife Agrippina, her 16-year-old son Nero was proclaimed emperor. His reign began promisingly but ended in tyranny, rebellion and his suicide in 68.

events.title: Philip IV of France orders the arrest of the Templars
events.description: In dawn raids across France, Philip IV's officers arrested hundreds of Knights Templar on charges of heresy and blasphemy. The heavily indebted king coveted their wealth, and the order was suppressed in 1312.

events.title: The cornerstone of the White House is laid
events.description: Freemasons laid the cornerstone of the President's House in the new federal city of Washington. Designed by James Hoban, it has housed every US president since John Adams.
events.html: Freemasons laid the cornerstone of the President's House in the new federal city of Washington. Designed by James Hoban, it has housed every US president since John Adams.

events.title: Greenwich is chosen as the world's prime meridian
events.description: Delegates at the International Meridian Conference in Washington voted to adopt the meridian through Greenwich as the zero of longitude. The decision underpins maps, navigation and the world's time zones.

events.title: Italy declares war on Germany
events.description: Five weeks after its armistice with the Allies, Pietro Badoglio's Italian government declared war on its former Axis partner. German forces nonetheless occupied northern and central Italy until 1945.
